entries.name: Interactive web design
entries.definition: Designing websites whose layout and elements respond to what visitors do, such as menus, forms, animation and live updates.

entries.name: Interactive web development
entries.definition: Writing the code that makes web pages respond to visitors' actions, usually with JavaScript.

entries.name: Interdisciplinary collaboration
entries.definition: Working effectively with people from other professions or fields, such as nurses and physicians or engineers and designers, toward a shared goal.

entries.name: Internal investigations
entries.definition: Investigating suspected misconduct or rule-breaking inside an organisation, such as fraud, harassment or policy breaches, to establish the facts and recommend action.

entries.name: International Standard Book Number
entries.definition: A unique number that identifies a particular edition of a book or similar publication, defined by the ISO 2108 standard.

entries.name: Internet Control Message Protocol
entries.definition: A network-layer protocol, defined in RFC 792, that IP devices use to send error messages and operational information, such as the echo requests used by ping.

entries.name: Internet Message Access Protocol
entries.definition: An email protocol that lets a mail client read and manage messages that stay stored on the mail server.

entries.name: Internet protocol suite
entries.definition: The set of communication protocols, such as IP, TCP and UDP, that computers use to exchange data over the internet and similar networks.

entries.name: Interpreting contracts under English law
entries.definition: Working out what the terms of a contract mean and how they apply under the law of England and Wales.

entries.name: Interpreting law
entries.definition: Working out what statutes, regulations and court decisions mean and how they apply to a particular situation.

entries.name: InterQual
entries.definition: A set of evidence-based clinical criteria, sold as software, that hospitals and insurers use in utilization review to judge whether admissions and levels of care are medically necessary.

entries.name: Intradermal injection
entries.definition: Injecting a small amount of a substance into the layer of skin just under the surface, as in a tuberculin skin test.

entries.name: Intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring
entries.definition: Using electrical tests such as EEG, evoked potentials and EMG during surgery to monitor the nervous system and warn the surgeon of possible injury.

entries.name: Intraoral cameras
entries.definition: Small pen-shaped cameras that dentists use to take enlarged pictures of the inside of a patient's mouth.

entries.name: Intravenous hydration
entries.definition: Giving fluids directly into a vein through an IV line to treat or prevent dehydration.

entries.name: Intravenous infusion
entries.definition: Giving fluids, medicines or nutrients into a vein through an IV line, using a drip or a pump.

entries.name: Inventory management software
entries.definition: Software for tracking stock levels, orders, sales and deliveries so that a business knows what it has and where.

entries.name: Investigating drug trafficking
entries.definition: Investigating the making, transport and sale of illegal drugs, including surveillance, informants, evidence gathering and tracing money.

entries.name: Investigative interviewing
entries.definition: Questioning witnesses, victims and suspects in a structured, non-coercive way to get accurate and complete accounts for an investigation.

entries.name: Investigator's brochure
entries.definition: Writing and maintaining the investigator's brochure, the document used in clinical trials that summarises the clinical and non-clinical data on the study drug for the people running the trial.

entries.name: InVision
entries.definition: A web-based digital product design platform for prototyping screens, collaborating on them and handing them off to developers, which was discontinued at the end of 2024.

entries.name: Invoice processing
entries.definition: Receiving, checking, recording and paying supplier invoices as part of accounts payable.

entries.name: Io.js
entries.definition: A fork of the Node.js JavaScript runtime, started in 2014 and merged back into Node.js in 2015.

entries.name: Ionic 2
entries.definition: The second major version of the Ionic framework for building mobile apps with web technologies, rebuilt on Angular to replace the AngularJS-based first version.

entries.name: iOS
entries.definition: The mobile operating system that Apple makes for the iPhone.

entries.name: IP address management
entries.definition: Planning, tracking and administering a network's IP address space and the DHCP and DNS records tied to it.

entries.name: IPython
entries.definition: An enhanced interactive Python shell, which also provides the kernel behind Jupyter notebooks.

entries.name: IronMQ
entries.definition: A hosted message-queue service from Iron.io for passing messages between the parts of an application.

entries.name: IronPython
entries.definition: An implementation of the Python language for the .NET platform.

entries.name: Irrigation (agriculture)
entries.definition: Supplying water to crops or land through channels, sprinklers or drip lines, and operating and maintaining the equipment that does so.

entries.name: Irrigation (health)
entries.definition: Flushing a wound, body cavity, eye, ear or catheter with a stream of sterile fluid to clean it or clear it out.

entries.name: ISO 10012
entries.definition: An ISO standard with requirements for managing measurement processes and the equipment used to measure.

entries.name: ISO 10993
entries.definition: A series of ISO standards for evaluating whether medical devices are biologically safe to use on or in the body.

entries.name: ISO 14000
entries.definition: A family of ISO standards on environmental management, of which ISO 14001 sets the requirements for an environmental management system.

entries.name: ISO 14971
entries.definition: An ISO standard describing how manufacturers identify, evaluate and control the risks of medical devices.

entries.name: ISO 15189
entries.definition: An ISO standard setting quality and competence requirements for medical laboratories.

entries.name: ISO 19011
entries.definition: An ISO standard giving guidance on auditing management systems, including how to plan audits and what auditors need to be competent in.

entries.name: ISO 26262
entries.definition: An ISO standard for the functional safety of electrical and electronic systems in road vehicles.

entries.name: ISO 31000
entries.definition: An ISO standard giving principles and guidelines for managing risk in any organisation.

entries.name: ISO 50001
entries.definition: An ISO standard with requirements for an energy management system that helps an organisation use energy more efficiently.
